With the switch on, sharing a photo goes straight to Chats. Refs #147.
- `Log chats that don't notify`, under `Keep a message log`, also saves messages from muted and restricted chats that aren't end-to-end encrypted, without a notification. Those chats used to stop before the log could see the message. Now they go through to the log and the notification is dropped right before it would show. Unsends still get marked, and auto reply leaves those chats alone. Refs #143.
- Patching in Morphe Manager holds less memory. One of the `Android Auto messages` lookups kept a copy of every APK it had read for as long as the patches stayed loaded, so patching a second time carried the first APK along. It lets go once it's done now. Refs #75.
- Patching does less work. The steps that look for chat heads, Material You colors and home screen shortcuts now skip code that can't match before reading it, and in testing on a computer a full patch used about a fifth less processor time. The patched app comes out exactly the same.
- Patching is quicker again. The step that finds where each switch goes used to read through Messenger's code once per switch, and now it reads it once for all of them. In testing on a computer a full patch took a little over half the processor time it did before, and the patched app is byte for byte the same.
- `GmsCore support` only tells Messenger that Google Play services is there while microG-RE is installed and turned on. It used to say yes either way, so without microG-RE Messenger kept reaching for an app that wasn't there. Now it carries on the way it does on a phone with no Play services. On Android 14 and newer, a phone without microG-RE also keeps Android's own sign-in route, so a password manager can still offer a saved login.
- A chat pinned with `Pin more chats` loses its pin mark as soon as you unpin it. The mark used to stay on the chat until Messenger restarted, even though Unpin had worked. Refs #56.

### Behind the scenes

- For developers, `scripts/CompatReport.java` is a small launcher now. The report it runs lives in `scripts/compat/`, one file per group of patches instead of one file of nearly 12,000 lines, and you start it the same way as before.

### Reports this release changed something for

#56, #75, #104, #120, #143, #145, #146, #147, #148, #149, #150, #151, #153, #154, #155, #156, #157, #158, #159, #160, #161, #162, #163, #166, #168, #169, #170, #172 and #173.

Full history is in the [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

### How to update

1. Update Messenger to 587.0.0.54.96 first. On [APKMirror's 587.0.0.54.96 page](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/facebook-2/messenger/facebook-messenger-587-0-0-54-96-release/), take a build whose version code is 347415262, 347415267, 347415268, 347415280, 347415281, 347415284, 347415285, 347415295, 347415299, 347415301, 347415302, 347415333, 347415337, 347415348, 347415350, 347415351, 347415352, 347415354 or 347415355. APKMirror shows the code for each download, and a build posted there after this release may not be supported yet.
2. In Morphe Manager (2.5.0 or newer), open **Sources** and refresh HushMessenger. The card should say **98 patches**.
3. Patch Messenger again and install it over your current one. Your settings carry over.

Patching on a computer? `patches-0.30.0.mpp` below is the same bundle for Morphe Desktop 2.1.0 or newer. It's a patch bundle, not a Messenger APK. `SHA256SUMS.txt` and its signature let you check the download, and the README says how.

### What was checked

- The full test suite, plus a patch run against all 19 Messenger 587.0.0.54.96 builds on file.
- Morphe Desktop patched and rebuilt one APK from each of the 4 build families.
- An APK patched from this exact bundle was installed on an emulator on Android API 32, signed in to Messenger. A chat, the inbox, both HushMessenger settings tabs, the message log, auto reply, Messenger's own settings, story settings and contact settings all opened, with no crashes.

hushfeed.title: v0.83.0
hushfeed.body:
Hushfeed v0.83.0 has 151 patches for global TikTok 47.8.3 (`com.zhiliaoapp.musically`). It's built on Morphe patcher 2.4.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.6.0 or newer before you patch (or use morphe-desktop 2.2.0 on a computer). Older ones won't load it.

TikTok moves to 47.8.3, so grab that build from APKMirror and patch it with the same signing key. Your login and settings carry over. You can watch a LIVE now without landing on its viewer list, or have mini dramas play in their own language instead of TikTok's AI dub. `Remove all comments` deletes every comment you've posted. Hushfeed's settings can also keep their own language and theme whatever TikTok is set to, and the app icon changes right from settings without patching again.

New in this release

- Hushfeed moves to TikTok 47.8.3, and only that one. 47.7.3 isn't supported anymore. Get the 47.8.3 bundle or APK from APKMirror and patch it with your usual signing key so your login and settings come along.
- You can switch the home screen icon from Hushfeed's settings now, without patching again (Discussion #114). Turn on `Pick the icon in Hushfeed` in the Custom launcher icon patch and an `App icon` row shows up under Appearance with every icon style, plus Your icon if you set a picture or a background color. Needs Android 8 or newer. Some home screens drop the icon when it changes, so if yours does, add TikTok back from the app list.
- `Liquid glass when held` makes the glass lens on the main feed's tabs react to your finger, the way the iPhone's tab bar does. Hold a finger on the tabs and the lens swells, then it wobbles back when you let go. With `Blur the video behind the bar` on Android 13 and up, the video under the lens bends harder while you hold it and splits into a little color at its edge. It works with or without `Slide across the tabs` and sits under `Glass lens on the current tab`.
- `Tap a video to remove it` (under Clean up your account on the Privacy page) turns a tap in your own Liked videos, Favorites or Reposts into a removal. The video dims while TikTok takes it back, then leaves the grid, and nothing opens. Other people's profiles and your own videos open as usual. It's off by default. (#401)
- `Remove all comments` and `Remove selected comments` are new on the Privacy page, under Clean up your account (#442). The first deletes every comment you've posted, one at a time with a short pause between them, and shows a count with Stop while it goes. The second opens your comment history so you can tick just the ones you want gone. Either way you get a few seconds with Cancel before anything is deleted.
- `Play original audio` plays mini dramas and other videos in their own language instead of the AI dub TikTok picks for your app language (#443). Captions and translations stay as they are, so you can keep TikTok in your language. Turn it on in Hushfeed settings > Playback. It's off by default.
- `Swipe left` has a new choice, `Save to a collection` (#445). A left swipe on a video opens TikTok's own popup for saving it to one of your collections, the same one you get by holding the Favorites button, so you never land on the creator's profile by accident. It works in Clear display too, where the buttons are hidden. Pick it under Hushfeed settings > Feed screen.
- `Group likes per comment` gives each comment or video people liked one row in the Inbox's Likes list, with everyone who liked it counted. TikTok's server only bundles the likes that come in close together, so a comment that keeps getting likes used to fill the list with rows like "A likes your comment" and "B, C and 5 others like your comment". Each row now sits where its newest like is, and older pages fold into it as you scroll. It starts off, sits under `Expand activity list` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox and applies the next time the Likes list loads. Thanks to @X-15 (#446).
- `Split activity list` turns the Inbox's Activity page into two of TikTok's own lists, your newest comments and replies on top and likes below, each scrolling and loading on its own, with the same Like and Reply buttons on each comment. TikTok mixes both into one list and puts likes it ranks as priority in front, so a reply to you could sit below twenty likes. The bar between the two lists stays put. Its ⇅ swaps which list is on top, its ✕ hides whichever list is below until the `Show` bar at the bottom brings it back, and Hushfeed remembers both. The Activity menu still works. Pick Likes, Comments or Mentions to see just that list, and Activity to get the split back. With `Search loaded activity` on, each list gets its own search bar. It starts off, sits under `Expand activity list` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox and applies the next time the page opens. Thanks to @X-15 (#447).
- Picked photo posts can come out as one video. With `Save photo posts as a video` on, pick two or more photo posts on a grid and tap Save, and you're asked whether you want one video or one per post. One video plays each post's photos in the order you picked them, each with its own sound, and any videos you picked still save on their own (#430).
- `Offer full screen in more LIVEs` gives LIVEs streamed from a phone the full screen button TikTok keeps for LIVEs from a computer or a shared screen. TikTok still shows it only when the stream is wide, and a tap turns the room sideways to fill the screen (#57).
- `LIVE name alerts` tells you when your name comes up in a LIVE. It catches chat lines that mention you or type your name, and in a room with captions on, your name said out loud. With TikTok's notifications on you get a notification that vibrates, and with them off a banner shows in the room. Your handle and TikTok name are always listened for, and `Names to listen for` adds the other names people call you. On Android 13 and newer, `Listen for your name` also listens to the LIVE's sound through your phone's own speech recognition, so a name said out loud counts in rooms without captions too. In a LIVE you're watching unseen, that listening starts once you tap the eye. They all sit under `Auto tap speed` in Hushfeed settings > Playback, with `LIVE controls` patched (#424).
- `Watch LIVEs unseen` keeps you off the viewer list of the LIVEs you open, so the host doesn't see you come in. The LIVE stays open and keeps playing while you're hidden, and doesn't skip ahead to the next one. A crossed-out eye in the room means you're hidden, and a tap on it lets that host see you until you close TikTok. It starts off and sits under Ghost mode in Hushfeed settings > Privacy (#420).
- Diagnostic reports get an `IMAGE LOADS` section. It counts the images TikTok fetched from each server since it started, how many of them failed and why, so a report can show what's behind covers and avatars that stay gray. Only the server's name goes in, never the image's address (#415).
- `Crop and stretch to fill the screen` covers the whole screen with a bit of both. It crops half as much as `Fill the screen with the video` and stretches half as much as `Stretch the video to the screen`, so neither one stands out. Turn it on in Hushfeed settings > Playback (#421).
- `Keep the middle unstretched` covers the whole screen and leaves the middle of the video at its own shape, so faces in the middle look normal. A little comes off each side, and the rest of the gap is made up along the top and bottom, stretched least where they meet the middle. It needs Android 13 or newer and asks for a restart, and until TikTok restarts it crops and stretches like `Crop and stretch to fill the screen` (#421).
- `Caption spot in Clear display` lets the caption you keep in Clear display sit lower, near the bottom, instead of up where TikTok puts it to clear the description. Clear display hides the description anyway, so the line doesn't have to float over an empty gap. `Caption height in Clear display` lifts it from whichever spot you pick. It's under `Keep captions in Clear display` in Hushfeed settings > Interface (#428).
- `Share the video after a save` opens Android's share sheet with the file as soon as a video is saved, video stories included, so you can send it straight to WhatsApp, Telegram or any other app without digging through your gallery. Photo posts you save as a video count too. Picked videos saved together still get the usual notice. It starts off and sits under `Show download progress` in Hushfeed settings > Downloads (#423).
- `Long-press Profile for Activity center` opens TikTok's Activity center when you hold the Profile tab, so your watch history, comments and time spent are one press away. A tap on Profile works as before, and while `Long-press Profile for Watch history` is on, that one keeps the press. If TikTok hasn't given your account an Activity center, the press opens Settings and privacy instead (#425).
- `Look up a commenter's country` adds Show account country to the menu you get by holding a comment. Tap it and you'll see where TikTok says that account is based. TikTok keeps that to itself for most accounts now, so you'll usually get the country its latest videos were posted from instead. The answer pops up at the bottom, and with `Show where commenters are from` on, that account's comments show it from then on. `Account country on profiles` puts the same lookup on a profile's share sheet as an Account country button. Both start off (#417, #201).
- `Hide the summary on LIVE previews` takes away the AI Summary card TikTok puts at the bottom of a LIVE in the feed, the one that sums up what the stream is about. Some LIVEs get a newer style of that card, and the switch hides that one too. It starts off and sits under `Hide the Service+ row under LIVE previews` in Hushfeed settings > Playback, with `LIVE controls` patched. Pausing Hushfeed shows the card again (#418).
- `Stretch the video to the screen` is a third choice under Playback, next to Fit and Fill. It covers the whole screen without cropping anything by making the video a little taller or wider. Videos far from your screen's shape stay as they are, so a landscape video never gets squashed into a tall one. It starts off, and turning it on turns the other two off (#406).
- `Hide Settings and privacy rows` takes TikTok's own rows you never use off its Settings and privacy page, like Ads or Shake to report. Tick them in the checklist under `Hide the Hushfeed row` in Hushfeed settings > App and they're gone the next time that page opens. A section that loses every row loses its title too, and pausing Hushfeed brings them all back (#244).
- `Show message times` puts the time each message was sent under it in a chat, in small gray text below the bubble. TikTok only shows a time above a message that comes after a gap. It starts off and sits under `Turn off swipe to reply` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox.
- `Glass Stories button on Following` swaps the flat gray Stories button at the top of the Following feed for glass with round ends, and on Android 12 and up the video behind it shows through blurred. It starts off and sits under `Hide the LIVE row on Following` in Hushfeed settings > Feed screen. Turning it off or pausing Hushfeed brings TikTok's own button back (#409).
- `Hide search result tabs` takes tabs you never use off the strip above search results. Tick Shop, LIVE, Places or any other tab TikTok shows you and it's gone from every search, while Top always stays. The checklist sits under `Hide TikTok Shop in search` in Hushfeed settings > Feed filter, and it shows each tab by name in your settings language.
- `Delete watched offline videos` clears the offline videos you've already watched every time TikTok starts, so the next download fills their spots with new ones. A video counts as watched once it's been on screen. It starts off, sits with the offline rows in Hushfeed settings > Downloads, and shows how many unwatched videos you have left.
- `Bottom bar height` makes TikTok's bottom bar shorter or taller, in five steps from Shorter to Taller. Videos and the other tabs make room for it at the new height. It sits under `Bottom bar icons` in Hushfeed settings > Feed tabs and takes hold after a restart.
- `Hide profile tabs` takes tabs off the strip above a profile's videos. Tick Videos, Reposts, Liked videos, Favorites, AI theater, Shop or any of the others and they're gone from every profile you open, yours included, so you can keep just Favorites and Liked if that's all you swipe between. With Videos hidden a profile opens on the first tab left, and at least one tab always stays. The checklist sits under `Hide profile shortcuts` in Hushfeed settings > App and takes hold after a restart (#392, #399).
- `Fix Spotify login` gets Add to Spotify past its sign-in. The Spotify app won't link a patched TikTok, so you now sign in on Spotify's own page inside TikTok and it links your account from there. It's on as soon as you patch it in, with no switch.
- The settings screen now comes in Arabic, shown when TikTok runs in Arabic. It's a first pass, so corrections from Arabic speakers are welcome (D307).
- `Video download codec` picks which codec a saved video comes in when TikTok has the same quality in both. Automatic keeps H.264, which nearly every player opens. HEVC first saves the HEVC copy, which is often sharper since TikTok can send its H.264 at a lower bitrate. H.264 only never saves HEVC, for older players and TVs. It sits under `Video download quality`. Thanks to @Tegar30 (#400).
- `Pick which stories to save` lets you save more than one of someone's stories at once. With it on, saving a story opens a checklist of their stories with the one you're watching already ticked, and a story you held to save waits, paused, until the list closes. Tick the others you want, or Pick all, and they save together with one progress count. TikTok loads a person's stories a few at a time as you watch, so the list says how many are still to come. It starts off and sits under `Save a story from its share sheet` in Hushfeed settings > Downloads (#393).
- `Check for already-saved videos` now covers the photo posts TikTok saves by itself too, on Android 10 and newer. That's live photos, plus still photos while `Download original photos` and `Save photo posts as a video` are both off. Save one twice and you get Open or Save again first, and the post gets its ✓ on profile grids like the rest (#197).
- `See-through status bar` now also works on videos you open from search, a profile or your Liked and Favorites. A new `Shade behind the status bar` puts a soft dark fade behind the clock and icons so they're still easy to read over a bright video. It's off to start with and sits right under `See-through status bar` (#407).
- `See-through bottom bar` runs the video all the way down under the gesture bar now. The feed used to stop just above it, so on phones with gesture navigation the handle sat on a black strip. The tabs, the caption and the buttons stay where they were. With `Fill the screen with the video` on, a video opened from search, a profile or your Liked videos goes under the gesture bar too, and its comment bar stays put (#408).
- `Export comments` now loads every reply under the comments first, so you don't have to open each thread by hand anymore. While it works, the count beside the buttons shows how many replies have come in and the button you tapped turns into Stop. Stopping, or closing the comments, saves what's loaded so far. The message after the export says when some replies didn't load, and a JSON file marks it with `replies_complete`. It stops at 3,000 replies. Every reply now sits right under its comment in the file, even ones you opened after scrolling further down, and if you leave TikTok while replies load, the save screen opens when you come back.
- Favorites grids get their own order. `Sort loaded videos on Favorites grids` starts at `Same as profile grids`, and the sort button on a Favorites grid now changes only that order, so Liked and your profile keep theirs. It sits right under the Liked row (#180).
- Collections you make inside Favorites can be sorted too. `Sort loaded videos in collections` starts at `Same as Favorites grids`, has the same orders, and a collection gets the sort button in its corner, which changes only the collection order. Open a video from a sorted collection and swiping up follows that order. A video pinned on its creator's profile sorts in with the rest there, and the collection's own top rows stay where they are (#180).
- `Show the country and date under the caption`, next to `Show the country as a flag`, puts the creator's country and the post date on a line of their own right below the caption, so the row with the name stays short. The line uses the same small print as the date, exact times and the saved mark included. Photo posts get the line too, and a post with no caption keeps both in the row. Turn it off and both go back where they were (#410).
- `Glass lens on the current tab` works on any bottom bar now, the glass one and every other style. Turn it on with whatever bar style you use, TikTok's own included, and the bubble sits behind your tab. `Slide across the tabs` and `Haptics on the tabs` come along with it. On a white bar the lens turns a soft gray so you can still see it, and TikTok's own bar color stays underneath (#416).
- The small window from `Keep watching in a small window` has previous and next buttons on both sides of play and pause, so you can move through the feed without opening TikTok. An arrow dims when there's no video that way. A tall video's window is too narrow for three buttons, so it shows play and next until you make it bigger. Leave a LIVE with the switch on and it keeps playing in TikTok's own small window, which TikTok hardly ever offered before. It works on tablets and foldables too, and on phones TikTok has mistaken for a tablet, which it used to leave out. When `Record LIVEs you watch` is on, that window gets a Record button next to its play and pause. Tap it again to stop, and the recording saves like one started from the room (#413).
- Feature Gate Lab has a `Visual search on paused videos` preset from Japan's builds. It turns on the search tag TikTok puts on things in a paused video, which opens its visual search. Like the other presets it needs the Lab's overrides switch and a TikTok restart, and TikTok's server still decides which videos get a tag (#98).
- `Day before month` writes the date by the creator's name day first, so 09-29 reads 29.09 and an older video's 2024-03-07 reads 07.03.24. Ages like 2d ago stay as they are. With `Show the time to the second` on, that date goes day first too, like 29.09.26 with `Short date` or 29 Sep 2026 without. It starts off and sits under `Short date` in Hushfeed settings > Interface (#438).
- Hushfeed's buttons on videos can be smaller or bigger now. `Size of the buttons on videos` goes from Smallest to Large, and `Line them up over the right column` stacks them above TikTok's own buttons on the right, starting over the avatar, so they move with that column instead of staying where you dragged them. Both sit right under the buttons in Hushfeed settings > Interface. `Hold TikTok's save button to download` makes a press and hold on TikTok's own save button save the video with your download settings, while a tap still adds it to Favorites. It sits under `Hold speed on Favorites` and needs `Long-press controls` and `Advanced downloads` patched (#433).
- `Settings theme` keeps Hushfeed's own settings and pop-ups dark or light whatever mode TikTok is in. `Match TikTok` is the old way and stays the default, while `Always dark` and `Always light` hold that look. The row is on the first page of Hushfeed settings, under `Pause Hushfeed`, and the page repaints as soon as you pick (#434).
- `Size of the LIVE buttons` makes Hushfeed's Record, Auto tap, Block and eye buttons in a LIVE room smaller, so they stop covering the room's own buttons on a small screen. Pick Small or Smallest in Hushfeed settings > Playback, under `Auto tap speed`. Normal keeps the size they've always had (#359).
- `Hushfeed language` shows Hushfeed's settings and messages in the language you pick, even when TikTok and your phone are set to another one. Each language is listed in its own name, and `Match TikTok` keeps the old way and stays the default. It's on the first page of Hushfeed settings, under `Settings theme` (#431).
- `Fill a tall screen instead`, right under `Fit the video to the screen`, gives a folding phone both looks. The tall front screen gets cropped to fill like `Fill the screen with the video`, while the big screen opened up (or a phone turned sideways) keeps the whole video. It switches as you fold and unfold (#345).
- `Save episodes button in the share sheet` puts Save episodes in the share sheet of a mini drama episode (#444). Tap it and you get that drama's episodes as a list, with the one you're watching already checked, so you can pick the ones you want and save them in one go. An episode you haven't unlocked only saves the short preview TikTok sends, and its row says so. Turn it on in Hushfeed settings > Downloads.
- `Hide LIVEs from accounts you don't follow` clears the LIVE circles TikTok mixes into the Inbox's stories tray from people you don't follow. LIVEs from accounts you follow stay put. `Hide the Widget circle` drops the circle at the end of the tray that pitches TikTok's home screen widget, and the widget itself keeps working. Both start off and sit under `Hide On this day` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox (#449).
- `Hide view counts on profile grids` takes the view count and its little play icon off every video on a profile grid. If you've turned on dates, lengths or the engagement rate for grids, they move up into that spot. It starts off and sits under `Show video length on profile grids` in Hushfeed settings > Feed screen (#449).

Bug Fixes

- TikTok no longer closes when it asks your screen for a slower refresh rate. `Keep the screen's refresh rate` had caught its own change of the rate along with TikTok's, so the first time TikTok asked, Hushfeed kept handing the request back to itself until TikTok crashed, with the switch on or off. TikTok doesn't ask on every phone, which is how it went unnoticed.
- On TikTok 47, switches that work by changing one of TikTok's own settings reach the copy TikTok reads again. TikTok 47 keeps those settings twice and reads almost all of them from the second copy, which Hushfeed didn't look at. That covers `Keep the Favorites tab`, `Use non-personalized search`, `Show the progress bar thumbnail` and `Stop the blink under the bar`, and lets `Keep the middle unstretched` work there. Feature Gate Lab rules on those settings take hold too (#448).
- `Hide surveys` catches the Not interested and Interested buttons under a video's description again when TikTok draws them from one of its templates, which got past both of the old checks. The diagnostic report also names what type each feed component was (#439).
- With `Open the comments at full height` on, TikTok's faded search icon no longer sits on top of the X that closes the comments. That icon belongs over the small video TikTok shows above the comments, and at full height there's no video up there for it (#435).
- The Advanced downloads description sent you to Downloads for `Show the save button on videos`, but the switch is in Feed screen under Buttons on videos. The description says where it is now, and Downloads has a row that takes you straight to it. Searching settings for "download button" finds it too (#299).
- The "Saving video" message doesn't sit on top of the saved banner anymore. It still did when another message was waiting behind it, like the sound's with `Save the sound as well` on. Where the sound went, and the notes about a watermarked copy or a possible second copy, are lines on the banner now (#299).
- With `Stretch the video to the screen` on, the still picture TikTok shows before a video starts gets stretched the same way as the video. It used to show a different shape and flick when the video took over (#421).
- With Ghost mode on, stories you watched stay watched after you close and reopen TikTok, in the inbox and on profiles. TikTok never heard you watched them, so their rings used to light up again once TikTok forgot the play (#427).
- `Show where a video was posted` no longer shows FAKE-AD on ads. TikTok gives ads a made up country, so only a real two-letter country shows now, and an ad's never gets remembered for that brand's comments (#410).
- With `Lock the hold speed with a pull down` on, pulling down while you hold the side of a video locks the speed again. The feed took that pull as a scroll back to the last video, or as a refresh on For You, and the hold ended before the lock could catch it. `Slide to change the hold speed` keeps its slide the same way, so a long slide no longer scrolls the feed out from under you (#422).
- With `Let other apps play until a video starts` on, backing out of a video you opened from a chat gives your music back as fast as leaving the feed does. It used to stay paused for about two seconds (#283).
- With `Stop video looping` on, the screen turns off on its usual timeout again once a video ends. TikTok keeps the screen lit for as long as the feed is open, so a phone left on a finished video never went dark. It stays on while anything plays (#414).
- Saving a photo post you've already saved now says the photo post is already saved, and a photo story says the story is. The choice to open it or save it again used to call it a video, even when you'd saved it as photos (#197).
- `Turn off haptics` also quiets Hushfeed's own buzzes now. Holding the For You, Home, Inbox or Profile tab and dragging the block button still vibrated with the switch on.
- `Fold long comments` folds comments that TikTok already cuts with its own "... more". Those used to stay at TikTok's six lines. Now our more opens TikTok's cut text, and TikTok's more opens the rest.
- When `Pause before the feed` or the daily hold comes up, TalkBack moves to its title and reads it. Coming back to TikTok from the home screen, TalkBack used to land on the Home tab and never said what was covering the feed. Once you've moved on to a button or a tab, pulling down the notification shade won't send you back to the title.
- `Stop analytics and tracking` now says it lets through the settings TikTok downloads to check its own requests. You'll still see that download in a network capture with the switch on, since TikTok's request checks read from it (#379).
- `Block location` also stops TikTok's own location lookup. Besides the phone's location services, TikTok asks location-v6.tiktokv.us, which works out where you are from your connection, and that request still went out with the switch on. With the switch on it's sent to your phone itself now, so it never leaves it (#379).
- In Simplified Chinese, the Lab's Apply button said 申请, which reads as applying for something. It says 应用 now.
- With a password on `Network proxy`, the small relay TikTok signs in through only connects to the domains TikTok uses. Another app on the phone could reach it while TikTok was open and send its own traffic through your proxy. Now it gets turned away.
- `Hide the Hushfeed row` only takes the row out of Settings and privacy while a hold on For You or Home opens Hushfeed settings. Hiding the feed tab strip or pointing For You at your watch history used to leave no way back in. Now the row stays until a long press works again (#244).
- `Fill the screen with the video` leaves wide and square videos whole. On a tall phone it used to zoom them in until they covered the screen, so you only saw the middle of a landscape video. Tall videos still lose the black strip under them (#394).
- `Foldable split comment view` puts comments beside the video after you unfold with TikTok open. TikTok rebuilt the feed for the wider screen but still reported the folded width, so comments kept opening over the video until a restart. Folding back now drops the side panel too (#398).
- A translated comment could still land in the wrong row when you scrolled fast. TikTok fades a translation in a moment after it arrives, and if the row got reused for another comment in that moment, the old comment's text was written over the new one. The fade is now called off when the row moves on (#383).
- Patching a TikTok APK that was compiled apart from the supported one stops right away with a message naming the file to get. APKMirror added one on November 12, the 47.7.3 APK marked arm64-v8a alone, and eight patches failed on it while others hooked the wrong code (#402).
- Two parts of TikTok reading the same new batch of feed videos at once could both run the feed filter on it and both rewrite it, and the second rewrite could crash TikTok while it was copying that batch. The filter now handles one batch at a time, so the second read finds it already done. Thanks to @Tegar30 for spotting it (#400).
- `Auto tap` in LIVE rooms with guests keeps its taps off the guests' seats. In a grid of guests, a tap on any seat opened that person's card or the gift panel and stopped the tapping, so now it taps the open room just above or below the seats instead (#335).
- `Foldable split comment view` works in a desktop window too, like TikTok on a Googlebook or Chromebook, in DeX or in Android's desktop mode. Those windows count as sharing the screen with other apps, so comments always came up from the bottom there, however wide the window or low the minimum width. Now the window's width decides, and dragging it across the minimum width switches the layout. Split screen still leaves comments to TikTok (#405).
- `Fill the screen with the video` reaches the bottom on videos you open from search, a profile or a grid too. The comment bar under those videos kept a solid black strip, so filling changed nothing there. Now the video runs all the way down behind the comment bar, and the caption and buttons stay above it (#406).
- `Blur the video behind the bar` lets go of a video once the pill isn't over it. Scroll slowly and the pill used to keep a blurred piece of the last video until the next one started playing. Now it goes back to plain glass right away (#408).
- Hushfeed settings and the Lab scroll on under the gesture bar instead of stopping at a solid band above it, and the last row still scrolls clear of the bar (#408).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the Blocked, Muted and Moderation lists in a LIVE's settings show their title, back arrow, help icon and Quit button in white. TikTok paints those in a fixed dark gray, so they almost vanished on the dark sheet. With `AMOLED dark theme` on, those lists are black now, like the Settings sheet they open from. They stayed gray unless you'd opened the LIVE from search (#362).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the tip that points at the creator's message button keeps its dark text on white. It had gone white on white (#362).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, a host's pinned comment looks the way it does with the switch off, its Pinned and timer tags included. Those tags came out in other colors over the darkened room (#362).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the Rose card that comes up the first time you tap a LIVE's quick gift reads white on its dark card. Its title and text stayed dark, so they almost vanished. The Request to join as a guest sheet goes black too, where its light text sat on a white sheet (#362).
- With a color picked in `AMOLED dark theme` and `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the box behind the delete key in a LIVE room's emoji picker takes that color too. It was the last spot in the picker still showing TikTok's own dark gray (#329).
- The block button and Hushfeed's other feed buttons go back to their spots after you close the picture-in-picture window and open TikTok again. They used to stay bunched up in the top corner over the feed tabs until you restarted TikTok (#413).
- The next and previous buttons in the picture-in-picture window play the video they move to. It used to sit on its first frame with no sound, and play and pause still went to the video you left. A LIVE in the way gets skipped, since it can't play in that window (#413).
- The Lab's `Scrolling comments on videos` preset now tells you where to look. TikTok only allows them on some wide videos, and those get an Add one-liner button under the video and a one-liner bar in full screen. The old note just said most videos stay the same (#98).
- `Show the time beside the progress bar` counts all the way to the video's length at the end. TikTok reports where a video is a few times a second, and the last report before the end came up to a third of a second short, so a 15 second video read 0:14 / 0:15 as auto scroll moved on and looked cut off a second early (#432).
- `Keep captions in Clear display` keeps the caption on screen after you swipe to the next video with Clear display still on. It only stayed on the first video you cleared, because TikTok clears the next video a moment before it says that video is playing (#428).
- `Floating bottom bar` and its glass look go pale where TikTok turns its tabs black, like on Home's Community grid. The dark pill used to stay put there, so the black icons sat on a gray smear. Now the pill and the glass turn white with a thin dark edge, the lens behind your tab goes gray to match, and they go dark again as soon as you're back on the videos (#436).
- `Stop analytics and tracking` also points TikTok's Orbu telemetry hosts, like proxy.telemetry, back at your phone, so their lookups never leave it. TikTok still looked them up on 47.7.3 with the switch on (#379).

Behind the scenes

- The patch tests that don't read the extension run in eight groups now, one per area (feed, playback, player, sharing, messages, look, the rest of the app) plus one for the tests that read the whole source tree. An area's classpath holds only the patch classes its tests reach, and its inputs only the sources they read. Change a patch and Gradle reruns the groups whose tests reach it and the shared one, while the rest stay up to date. An edit to Hide profile tabs took 14 minutes instead of the full run's 39. Settings and navigation code reaches every group, so an edit there still reruns all of them. A full run still runs every group, and a group that finds no tests on a full run fails it.
- The patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.4.0 now, so the next bundle needs Morphe Manager 2.6.0 or newer, or morphe-desktop 2.2.0 from a computer. Older Managers won't load it.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.6.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfeed source.
2. Patch TikTok 47.8.3 from APKMirror. Keep the manager's existing signing key so your login and settings carry over.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a TikTok APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed#install).

What was checked

* All 151 TikTok patches applied to TikTok 47.8.3 with none failing.
* This exact bundle was patched onto TikTok 47.8.3 and run on a signed-in Galaxy S22. A walk through the whole app opened 27 screens with no crash.
- `Keep the screen's refresh rate` with TikTok forced to ask for 30 Hz: no request with the switch on, the 30 Hz request with it off, and no crash either way.

repos.title: v0.83.0
repos.body:
Hushfeed v0.83.0 has 151 patches for global TikTok 47.8.3 (`com.zhiliaoapp.musically`). It's built on Morphe patcher 2.4.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.6.0 or newer before you patch (or use morphe-desktop 2.2.0 on a computer). Older ones won't load it.

TikTok moves to 47.8.3, so grab that build from APKMirror and patch it with the same signing key. Your login and settings carry over. You can watch a LIVE now without landing on its viewer list, or have mini dramas play in their own language instead of TikTok's AI dub. `Remove all comments` deletes every comment you've posted. Hushfeed's settings can also keep their own language and theme whatever TikTok is set to, and the app icon changes right from settings without patching again.

New in this release

- Hushfeed moves to TikTok 47.8.3, and only that one. 47.7.3 isn't supported anymore. Get the 47.8.3 bundle or APK from APKMirror and patch it with your usual signing key so your login and settings come along.
- You can switch the home screen icon from Hushfeed's settings now, without patching again (Discussion #114). Turn on `Pick the icon in Hushfeed` in the Custom launcher icon patch and an `App icon` row shows up under Appearance with every icon style, plus Your icon if you set a picture or a background color. Needs Android 8 or newer. Some home screens drop the icon when it changes, so if yours does, add TikTok back from the app list.
- `Liquid glass when held` makes the glass lens on the main feed's tabs react to your finger, the way the iPhone's tab bar does. Hold a finger on the tabs and the lens swells, then it wobbles back when you let go. With `Blur the video behind the bar` on Android 13 and up, the video under the lens bends harder while you hold it and splits into a little color at its edge. It works with or without `Slide across the tabs` and sits under `Glass lens on the current tab`.
- `Tap a video to remove it` (under Clean up your account on the Privacy page) turns a tap in your own Liked videos, Favorites or Reposts into a removal. The video dims while TikTok takes it back, then leaves the grid, and nothing opens. Other people's profiles and your own videos open as usual. It's off by default. (#401)
- `Remove all comments` and `Remove selected comments` are new on the Privacy page, under Clean up your account (#442). The first deletes every comment you've posted, one at a time with a short pause between them, and shows a count with Stop while it goes. The second opens your comment history so you can tick just the ones you want gone. Either way you get a few seconds with Cancel before anything is deleted.
- `Play original audio` plays mini dramas and other videos in their own language instead of the AI dub TikTok picks for your app language (#443). Captions and translations stay as they are, so you can keep TikTok in your language. Turn it on in Hushfeed settings > Playback. It's off by default.
- `Swipe left` has a new choice, `Save to a collection` (#445). A left swipe on a video opens TikTok's own popup for saving it to one of your collections, the same one you get by holding the Favorites button, so you never land on the creator's profile by accident. It works in Clear display too, where the buttons are hidden. Pick it under Hushfeed settings > Feed screen.
- `Group likes per comment` gives each comment or video people liked one row in the Inbox's Likes list, with everyone who liked it counted. TikTok's server only bundles the likes that come in close together, so a comment that keeps getting likes used to fill the list with rows like "A likes your comment" and "B, C and 5 others like your comment". Each row now sits where its newest like is, and older pages fold into it as you scroll. It starts off, sits under `Expand activity list` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox and applies the next time the Likes list loads. Thanks to @X-15 (#446).
- `Split activity list` turns the Inbox's Activity page into two of TikTok's own lists, your newest comments and replies on top and likes below, each scrolling and loading on its own, with the same Like and Reply buttons on each comment. TikTok mixes both into one list and puts likes it ranks as priority in front, so a reply to you could sit below twenty likes. The bar between the two lists stays put. Its ⇅ swaps which list is on top, its ✕ hides whichever list is below until the `Show` bar at the bottom brings it back, and Hushfeed remembers both. The Activity menu still works. Pick Likes, Comments or Mentions to see just that list, and Activity to get the split back. With `Search loaded activity` on, each list gets its own search bar. It starts off, sits under `Expand activity list` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox and applies the next time the page opens. Thanks to @X-15 (#447).
- Picked photo posts can come out as one video. With `Save photo posts as a video` on, pick two or more photo posts on a grid and tap Save, and you're asked whether you want one video or one per post. One video plays each post's photos in the order you picked them, each with its own sound, and any videos you picked still save on their own (#430).
- `Offer full screen in more LIVEs` gives LIVEs streamed from a phone the full screen button TikTok keeps for LIVEs from a computer or a shared screen. TikTok still shows it only when the stream is wide, and a tap turns the room sideways to fill the screen (#57).
- `LIVE name alerts` tells you when your name comes up in a LIVE. It catches chat lines that mention you or type your name, and in a room with captions on, your name said out loud. With TikTok's notifications on you get a notification that vibrates, and with them off a banner shows in the room. Your handle and TikTok name are always listened for, and `Names to listen for` adds the other names people call you. On Android 13 and newer, `Listen for your name` also listens to the LIVE's sound through your phone's own speech recognition, so a name said out loud counts in rooms without captions too. In a LIVE you're watching unseen, that listening starts once you tap the eye. They all sit under `Auto tap speed` in Hushfeed settings > Playback, with `LIVE controls` patched (#424).
- `Watch LIVEs unseen` keeps you off the viewer list of the LIVEs you open, so the host doesn't see you come in. The LIVE stays open and keeps playing while you're hidden, and doesn't skip ahead to the next one. A crossed-out eye in the room means you're hidden, and a tap on it lets that host see you until you close TikTok. It starts off and sits under Ghost mode in Hushfeed settings > Privacy (#420).
- Diagnostic reports get an `IMAGE LOADS` section. It counts the images TikTok fetched from each server since it started, how many of them failed and why, so a report can show what's behind covers and avatars that stay gray. Only the server's name goes in, never the image's address (#415).
- `Crop and stretch to fill the screen` covers the whole screen with a bit of both. It crops half as much as `Fill the screen with the video` and stretches half as much as `Stretch the video to the screen`, so neither one stands out. Turn it on in Hushfeed settings > Playback (#421).
- `Keep the middle unstretched` covers the whole screen and leaves the middle of the video at its own shape, so faces in the middle look normal. A little comes off each side, and the rest of the gap is made up along the top and bottom, stretched least where they meet the middle. It needs Android 13 or newer and asks for a restart, and until TikTok restarts it crops and stretches like `Crop and stretch to fill the screen` (#421).
- `Caption spot in Clear display` lets the caption you keep in Clear display sit lower, near the bottom, instead of up where TikTok puts it to clear the description. Clear display hides the description anyway, so the line doesn't have to float over an empty gap. `Caption height in Clear display` lifts it from whichever spot you pick. It's under `Keep captions in Clear display` in Hushfeed settings > Interface (#428).
- `Share the video after a save` opens Android's share sheet with the file as soon as a video is saved, video stories included, so you can send it straight to WhatsApp, Telegram or any other app without digging through your gallery. Photo posts you save as a video count too. Picked videos saved together still get the usual notice. It starts off and sits under `Show download progress` in Hushfeed settings > Downloads (#423).
- `Long-press Profile for Activity center` opens TikTok's Activity center when you hold the Profile tab, so your watch history, comments and time spent are one press away. A tap on Profile works as before, and while `Long-press Profile for Watch history` is on, that one keeps the press. If TikTok hasn't given your account an Activity center, the press opens Settings and privacy instead (#425).
- `Look up a commenter's country` adds Show account country to the menu you get by holding a comment. Tap it and you'll see where TikTok says that account is based. TikTok keeps that to itself for most accounts now, so you'll usually get the country its latest videos were posted from instead. The answer pops up at the bottom, and with `Show where commenters are from` on, that account's comments show it from then on. `Account country on profiles` puts the same lookup on a profile's share sheet as an Account country button. Both start off (#417, #201).
- `Hide the summary on LIVE previews` takes away the AI Summary card TikTok puts at the bottom of a LIVE in the feed, the one that sums up what the stream is about. Some LIVEs get a newer style of that card, and the switch hides that one too. It starts off and sits under `Hide the Service+ row under LIVE previews` in Hushfeed settings > Playback, with `LIVE controls` patched. Pausing Hushfeed shows the card again (#418).
- `Stretch the video to the screen` is a third choice under Playback, next to Fit and Fill. It covers the whole screen without cropping anything by making the video a little taller or wider. Videos far from your screen's shape stay as they are, so a landscape video never gets squashed into a tall one. It starts off, and turning it on turns the other two off (#406).
- `Hide Settings and privacy rows` takes TikTok's own rows you never use off its Settings and privacy page, like Ads or Shake to report. Tick them in the checklist under `Hide the Hushfeed row` in Hushfeed settings > App and they're gone the next time that page opens. A section that loses every row loses its title too, and pausing Hushfeed brings them all back (#244).
- `Show message times` puts the time each message was sent under it in a chat, in small gray text below the bubble. TikTok only shows a time above a message that comes after a gap. It starts off and sits under `Turn off swipe to reply` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox.
- `Glass Stories button on Following` swaps the flat gray Stories button at the top of the Following feed for glass with round ends, and on Android 12 and up the video behind it shows through blurred. It starts off and sits under `Hide the LIVE row on Following` in Hushfeed settings > Feed screen. Turning it off or pausing Hushfeed brings TikTok's own button back (#409).
- `Hide search result tabs` takes tabs you never use off the strip above search results. Tick Shop, LIVE, Places or any other tab TikTok shows you and it's gone from every search, while Top always stays. The checklist sits under `Hide TikTok Shop in search` in Hushfeed settings > Feed filter, and it shows each tab by name in your settings language.
- `Delete watched offline videos` clears the offline videos you've already watched every time TikTok starts, so the next download fills their spots with new ones. A video counts as watched once it's been on screen. It starts off, sits with the offline rows in Hushfeed settings > Downloads, and shows how many unwatched videos you have left.
- `Bottom bar height` makes TikTok's bottom bar shorter or taller, in five steps from Shorter to Taller. Videos and the other tabs make room for it at the new height. It sits under `Bottom bar icons` in Hushfeed settings > Feed tabs and takes hold after a restart.
- `Hide profile tabs` takes tabs off the strip above a profile's videos. Tick Videos, Reposts, Liked videos, Favorites, AI theater, Shop or any of the others and they're gone from every profile you open, yours included, so you can keep just Favorites and Liked if that's all you swipe between. With Videos hidden a profile opens on the first tab left, and at least one tab always stays. The checklist sits under `Hide profile shortcuts` in Hushfeed settings > App and takes hold after a restart (#392, #399).
- `Fix Spotify login` gets Add to Spotify past its sign-in. The Spotify app won't link a patched TikTok, so you now sign in on Spotify's own page inside TikTok and it links your account from there. It's on as soon as you patch it in, with no switch.
- The settings screen now comes in Arabic, shown when TikTok runs in Arabic. It's a first pass, so corrections from Arabic speakers are welcome (D307).
- `Video download codec` picks which codec a saved video comes in when TikTok has the same quality in both. Automatic keeps H.264, which nearly every player opens. HEVC first saves the HEVC copy, which is often sharper since TikTok can send its H.264 at a lower bitrate. H.264 only never saves HEVC, for older players and TVs. It sits under `Video download quality`. Thanks to @Tegar30 (#400).
- `Pick which stories to save` lets you save more than one of someone's stories at once. With it on, saving a story opens a checklist of their stories with the one you're watching already ticked, and a story you held to save waits, paused, until the list closes. Tick the others you want, or Pick all, and they save together with one progress count. TikTok loads a person's stories a few at a time as you watch, so the list says how many are still to come. It starts off and sits under `Save a story from its share sheet` in Hushfeed settings > Downloads (#393).
- `Check for already-saved videos` now covers the photo posts TikTok saves by itself too, on Android 10 and newer. That's live photos, plus still photos while `Download original photos` and `Save photo posts as a video` are both off. Save one twice and you get Open or Save again first, and the post gets its ✓ on profile grids like the rest (#197).
- `See-through status bar` now also works on videos you open from search, a profile or your Liked and Favorites. A new `Shade behind the status bar` puts a soft dark fade behind the clock and icons so they're still easy to read over a bright video. It's off to start with and sits right under `See-through status bar` (#407).
- `See-through bottom bar` runs the video all the way down under the gesture bar now. The feed used to stop just above it, so on phones with gesture navigation the handle sat on a black strip. The tabs, the caption and the buttons stay where they were. With `Fill the screen with the video` on, a video opened from search, a profile or your Liked videos goes under the gesture bar too, and its comment bar stays put (#408).
- `Export comments` now loads every reply under the comments first, so you don't have to open each thread by hand anymore. While it works, the count beside the buttons shows how many replies have come in and the button you tapped turns into Stop. Stopping, or closing the comments, saves what's loaded so far. The message after the export says when some replies didn't load, and a JSON file marks it with `replies_complete`. It stops at 3,000 replies. Every reply now sits right under its comment in the file, even ones you opened after scrolling further down, and if you leave TikTok while replies load, the save screen opens when you come back.
- Favorites grids get their own order. `Sort loaded videos on Favorites grids` starts at `Same as profile grids`, and the sort button on a Favorites grid now changes only that order, so Liked and your profile keep theirs. It sits right under the Liked row (#180).
- Collections you make inside Favorites can be sorted too. `Sort loaded videos in collections` starts at `Same as Favorites grids`, has the same orders, and a collection gets the sort button in its corner, which changes only the collection order. Open a video from a sorted collection and swiping up follows that order. A video pinned on its creator's profile sorts in with the rest there, and the collection's own top rows stay where they are (#180).
- `Show the country and date under the caption`, next to `Show the country as a flag`, puts the creator's country and the post date on a line of their own right below the caption, so the row with the name stays short. The line uses the same small print as the date, exact times and the saved mark included. Photo posts get the line too, and a post with no caption keeps both in the row. Turn it off and both go back where they were (#410).
- `Glass lens on the current tab` works on any bottom bar now, the glass one and every other style. Turn it on with whatever bar style you use, TikTok's own included, and the bubble sits behind your tab. `Slide across the tabs` and `Haptics on the tabs` come along with it. On a white bar the lens turns a soft gray so you can still see it, and TikTok's own bar color stays underneath (#416).
- The small window from `Keep watching in a small window` has previous and next buttons on both sides of play and pause, so you can move through the feed without opening TikTok. An arrow dims when there's no video that way. A tall video's window is too narrow for three buttons, so it shows play and next until you make it bigger. Leave a LIVE with the switch on and it keeps playing in TikTok's own small window, which TikTok hardly ever offered before. It works on tablets and foldables too, and on phones TikTok has mistaken for a tablet, which it used to leave out. When `Record LIVEs you watch` is on, that window gets a Record button next to its play and pause. Tap it again to stop, and the recording saves like one started from the room (#413).
- Feature Gate Lab has a `Visual search on paused videos` preset from Japan's builds. It turns on the search tag TikTok puts on things in a paused video, which opens its visual search. Like the other presets it needs the Lab's overrides switch and a TikTok restart, and TikTok's server still decides which videos get a tag (#98).
- `Day before month` writes the date by the creator's name day first, so 09-29 reads 29.09 and an older video's 2024-03-07 reads 07.03.24. Ages like 2d ago stay as they are. With `Show the time to the second` on, that date goes day first too, like 29.09.26 with `Short date` or 29 Sep 2026 without. It starts off and sits under `Short date` in Hushfeed settings > Interface (#438).
- Hushfeed's buttons on videos can be smaller or bigger now. `Size of the buttons on videos` goes from Smallest to Large, and `Line them up over the right column` stacks them above TikTok's own buttons on the right, starting over the avatar, so they move with that column instead of staying where you dragged them. Both sit right under the buttons in Hushfeed settings > Interface. `Hold TikTok's save button to download` makes a press and hold on TikTok's own save button save the video with your download settings, while a tap still adds it to Favorites. It sits under `Hold speed on Favorites` and needs `Long-press controls` and `Advanced downloads` patched (#433).
- `Settings theme` keeps Hushfeed's own settings and pop-ups dark or light whatever mode TikTok is in. `Match TikTok` is the old way and stays the default, while `Always dark` and `Always light` hold that look. The row is on the first page of Hushfeed settings, under `Pause Hushfeed`, and the page repaints as soon as you pick (#434).
- `Size of the LIVE buttons` makes Hushfeed's Record, Auto tap, Block and eye buttons in a LIVE room smaller, so they stop covering the room's own buttons on a small screen. Pick Small or Smallest in Hushfeed settings > Playback, under `Auto tap speed`. Normal keeps the size they've always had (#359).
- `Hushfeed language` shows Hushfeed's settings and messages in the language you pick, even when TikTok and your phone are set to another one. Each language is listed in its own name, and `Match TikTok` keeps the old way and stays the default. It's on the first page of Hushfeed settings, under `Settings theme` (#431).
- `Fill a tall screen instead`, right under `Fit the video to the screen`, gives a folding phone both looks. The tall front screen gets cropped to fill like `Fill the screen with the video`, while the big screen opened up (or a phone turned sideways) keeps the whole video. It switches as you fold and unfold (#345).
- `Save episodes button in the share sheet` puts Save episodes in the share sheet of a mini drama episode (#444). Tap it and you get that drama's episodes as a list, with the one you're watching already checked, so you can pick the ones you want and save them in one go. An episode you haven't unlocked only saves the short preview TikTok sends, and its row says so. Turn it on in Hushfeed settings > Downloads.
- `Hide LIVEs from accounts you don't follow` clears the LIVE circles TikTok mixes into the Inbox's stories tray from people you don't follow. LIVEs from accounts you follow stay put. `Hide the Widget circle` drops the circle at the end of the tray that pitches TikTok's home screen widget, and the widget itself keeps working. Both start off and sit under `Hide On this day` in Hushfeed settings > Inbox (#449).
- `Hide view counts on profile grids` takes the view count and its little play icon off every video on a profile grid. If you've turned on dates, lengths or the engagement rate for grids, they move up into that spot. It starts off and sits under `Show video length on profile grids` in Hushfeed settings > Feed screen (#449).

Bug Fixes

- TikTok no longer closes when it asks your screen for a slower refresh rate. `Keep the screen's refresh rate` had caught its own change of the rate along with TikTok's, so the first time TikTok asked, Hushfeed kept handing the request back to itself until TikTok crashed, with the switch on or off. TikTok doesn't ask on every phone, which is how it went unnoticed.
- On TikTok 47, switches that work by changing one of TikTok's own settings reach the copy TikTok reads again. TikTok 47 keeps those settings twice and reads almost all of them from the second copy, which Hushfeed didn't look at. That covers `Keep the Favorites tab`, `Use non-personalized search`, `Show the progress bar thumbnail` and `Stop the blink under the bar`, and lets `Keep the middle unstretched` work there. Feature Gate Lab rules on those settings take hold too (#448).
- `Hide surveys` catches the Not interested and Interested buttons under a video's description again when TikTok draws them from one of its templates, which got past both of the old checks. The diagnostic report also names what type each feed component was (#439).
- With `Open the comments at full height` on, TikTok's faded search icon no longer sits on top of the X that closes the comments. That icon belongs over the small video TikTok shows above the comments, and at full height there's no video up there for it (#435).
- The Advanced downloads description sent you to Downloads for `Show the save button on videos`, but the switch is in Feed screen under Buttons on videos. The description says where it is now, and Downloads has a row that takes you straight to it. Searching settings for "download button" finds it too (#299).
- The "Saving video" message doesn't sit on top of the saved banner anymore. It still did when another message was waiting behind it, like the sound's with `Save the sound as well` on. Where the sound went, and the notes about a watermarked copy or a possible second copy, are lines on the banner now (#299).
- With `Stretch the video to the screen` on, the still picture TikTok shows before a video starts gets stretched the same way as the video. It used to show a different shape and flick when the video took over (#421).
- With Ghost mode on, stories you watched stay watched after you close and reopen TikTok, in the inbox and on profiles. TikTok never heard you watched them, so their rings used to light up again once TikTok forgot the play (#427).
- `Show where a video was posted` no longer shows FAKE-AD on ads. TikTok gives ads a made up country, so only a real two-letter country shows now, and an ad's never gets remembered for that brand's comments (#410).
- With `Lock the hold speed with a pull down` on, pulling down while you hold the side of a video locks the speed again. The feed took that pull as a scroll back to the last video, or as a refresh on For You, and the hold ended before the lock could catch it. `Slide to change the hold speed` keeps its slide the same way, so a long slide no longer scrolls the feed out from under you (#422).
- With `Let other apps play until a video starts` on, backing out of a video you opened from a chat gives your music back as fast as leaving the feed does. It used to stay paused for about two seconds (#283).
- With `Stop video looping` on, the screen turns off on its usual timeout again once a video ends. TikTok keeps the screen lit for as long as the feed is open, so a phone left on a finished video never went dark. It stays on while anything plays (#414).
- Saving a photo post you've already saved now says the photo post is already saved, and a photo story says the story is. The choice to open it or save it again used to call it a video, even when you'd saved it as photos (#197).
- `Turn off haptics` also quiets Hushfeed's own buzzes now. Holding the For You, Home, Inbox or Profile tab and dragging the block button still vibrated with the switch on.
- `Fold long comments` folds comments that TikTok already cuts with its own "... more". Those used to stay at TikTok's six lines. Now our more opens TikTok's cut text, and TikTok's more opens the rest.
- When `Pause before the feed` or the daily hold comes up, TalkBack moves to its title and reads it. Coming back to TikTok from the home screen, TalkBack used to land on the Home tab and never said what was covering the feed. Once you've moved on to a button or a tab, pulling down the notification shade won't send you back to the title.
- `Stop analytics and tracking` now says it lets through the settings TikTok downloads to check its own requests. You'll still see that download in a network capture with the switch on, since TikTok's request checks read from it (#379).
- `Block location` also stops TikTok's own location lookup. Besides the phone's location services, TikTok asks location-v6.tiktokv.us, which works out where you are from your connection, and that request still went out with the switch on. With the switch on it's sent to your phone itself now, so it never leaves it (#379).
- In Simplified Chinese, the Lab's Apply button said 申请, which reads as applying for something. It says 应用 now.
- With a password on `Network proxy`, the small relay TikTok signs in through only connects to the domains TikTok uses. Another app on the phone could reach it while TikTok was open and send its own traffic through your proxy. Now it gets turned away.
- `Hide the Hushfeed row` only takes the row out of Settings and privacy while a hold on For You or Home opens Hushfeed settings. Hiding the feed tab strip or pointing For You at your watch history used to leave no way back in. Now the row stays until a long press works again (#244).
- `Fill the screen with the video` leaves wide and square videos whole. On a tall phone it used to zoom them in until they covered the screen, so you only saw the middle of a landscape video. Tall videos still lose the black strip under them (#394).
- `Foldable split comment view` puts comments beside the video after you unfold with TikTok open. TikTok rebuilt the feed for the wider screen but still reported the folded width, so comments kept opening over the video until a restart. Folding back now drops the side panel too (#398).
- A translated comment could still land in the wrong row when you scrolled fast. TikTok fades a translation in a moment after it arrives, and if the row got reused for another comment in that moment, the old comment's text was written over the new one. The fade is now called off when the row moves on (#383).
- Patching a TikTok APK that was compiled apart from the supported one stops right away with a message naming the file to get. APKMirror added one on November 12, the 47.7.3 APK marked arm64-v8a alone, and eight patches failed on it while others hooked the wrong code (#402).
- Two parts of TikTok reading the same new batch of feed videos at once could both run the feed filter on it and both rewrite it, and the second rewrite could crash TikTok while it was copying that batch. The filter now handles one batch at a time, so the second read finds it already done. Thanks to @Tegar30 for spotting it (#400).
- `Auto tap` in LIVE rooms with guests keeps its taps off the guests' seats. In a grid of guests, a tap on any seat opened that person's card or the gift panel and stopped the tapping, so now it taps the open room just above or below the seats instead (#335).
- `Foldable split comment view` works in a desktop window too, like TikTok on a Googlebook or Chromebook, in DeX or in Android's desktop mode. Those windows count as sharing the screen with other apps, so comments always came up from the bottom there, however wide the window or low the minimum width. Now the window's width decides, and dragging it across the minimum width switches the layout. Split screen still leaves comments to TikTok (#405).
- `Fill the screen with the video` reaches the bottom on videos you open from search, a profile or a grid too. The comment bar under those videos kept a solid black strip, so filling changed nothing there. Now the video runs all the way down behind the comment bar, and the caption and buttons stay above it (#406).
- `Blur the video behind the bar` lets go of a video once the pill isn't over it. Scroll slowly and the pill used to keep a blurred piece of the last video until the next one started playing. Now it goes back to plain glass right away (#408).
- Hushfeed settings and the Lab scroll on under the gesture bar instead of stopping at a solid band above it, and the last row still scrolls clear of the bar (#408).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the Blocked, Muted and Moderation lists in a LIVE's settings show their title, back arrow, help icon and Quit button in white. TikTok paints those in a fixed dark gray, so they almost vanished on the dark sheet. With `AMOLED dark theme` on, those lists are black now, like the Settings sheet they open from. They stayed gray unless you'd opened the LIVE from search (#362).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the tip that points at the creator's message button keeps its dark text on white. It had gone white on white (#362).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, a host's pinned comment looks the way it does with the switch off, its Pinned and timer tags included. Those tags came out in other colors over the darkened room (#362).
- With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the Rose card that comes up the first time you tap a LIVE's quick gift reads white on its dark card. Its title and text stayed dark, so they almost vanished. The Request to join as a guest sheet goes black too, where its light text sat on a white sheet (#362).
- With a color picked in `AMOLED dark theme` and `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the box behind the delete key in a LIVE room's emoji picker takes that color too. It was the last spot in the picker still showing TikTok's own dark gray (#329).
- The block button and Hushfeed's other feed buttons go back to their spots after you close the picture-in-picture window and open TikTok again. They used to stay bunched up in the top corner over the feed tabs until you restarted TikTok (#413).
- The next and previous buttons in the picture-in-picture window play the video they move to. It used to sit on its first frame with no sound, and play and pause still went to the video you left. A LIVE in the way gets skipped, since it can't play in that window (#413).
- The Lab's `Scrolling comments on videos` preset now tells you where to look. TikTok only allows them on some wide videos, and those get an Add one-liner button under the video and a one-liner bar in full screen. The old note just said most videos stay the same (#98).
- `Show the time beside the progress bar` counts all the way to the video's length at the end. TikTok reports where a video is a few times a second, and the last report before the end came up to a third of a second short, so a 15 second video read 0:14 / 0:15 as auto scroll moved on and looked cut off a second early (#432).
- `Keep captions in Clear display` keeps the caption on screen after you swipe to the next video with Clear display still on. It only stayed on the first video you cleared, because TikTok clears the next video a moment before it says that video is playing (#428).
- `Floating bottom bar` and its glass look go pale where TikTok turns its tabs black, like on Home's Community grid. The dark pill used to stay put there, so the black icons sat on a gray smear. Now the pill and the glass turn white with a thin dark edge, the lens behind your tab goes gray to match, and they go dark again as soon as you're back on the videos (#436).
- `Stop analytics and tracking` also points TikTok's Orbu telemetry hosts, like proxy.telemetry, back at your phone, so their lookups never leave it. TikTok still looked them up on 47.7.3 with the switch on (#379).

Behind the scenes

- The patch tests that don't read the extension run in eight groups now, one per area (feed, playback, player, sharing, messages, look, the rest of the app) plus one for the tests that read the whole source tree. An area's classpath holds only the patch classes its tests reach, and its inputs only the sources they read. Change a patch and Gradle reruns the groups whose tests reach it and the shared one, while the rest stay up to date. An edit to Hide profile tabs took 14 minutes instead of the full run's 39. Settings and navigation code reaches every group, so an edit there still reruns all of them. A full run still runs every group, and a group that finds no tests on a full run fails it.
- The patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.4.0 now, so the next bundle needs Morphe Manager 2.6.0 or newer, or morphe-desktop 2.2.0 from a computer. Older Managers won't load it.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.6.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfeed source.
2. Patch TikTok 47.8.3 from APKMirror. Keep the manager's existing signing key so your login and settings carry over.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a TikTok APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/hushfeed#install).

What was checked

* All 151 TikTok patches applied to TikTok 47.8.3 with none failing.
* This exact bundle was patched onto TikTok 47.8.3 and run on a signed-in Galaxy S22. A walk through the whole app opened 27 screens with no crash.
- `Keep the screen's refresh rate` with TikTok forced to ask for 30 Hz: no request with the switch on, the 30 Hz request with it off, and no crash either way.
